text: Admission Mapping Rules
The admission-mapping process compares each student in the school file with the reference dump. The following rules are applied in order.
Check that all required columns are available in both the school file and the dump.
Remove completely identical rows from the school file. One copy is kept.
Clean the values before comparison:
Remove extra spaces.
Convert admission numbers and first names to lowercase.
Keep leading zeros. For example, 00123 and 123 are treated as different admission numbers.
Prepare the dump for searching and count how many times each admission number appears.
Check each school record:
If the admission number is blank → Not Matched
If the same admission number appears in multiple school records → Review
If the school first name is blank → Review
If the admission number appears multiple times in the dump → Review
If the admission number is not found in the dump → Not Matched
If the dump first name is blank → Review
If the school first name and dump first name do not match → Review
If the matching first name contains only one character → Review
If the username is missing from the dump → Review
If the admission number and first name match and the username is available → Matched
For matched records, copy the username and user ID from the dump.
Perform a final duplicate-account check:
If multiple matched records have the same username, move them to Review.
If multiple matched records have the same user ID, move them to Review.
Separate the final records into three groups:
Matched
Review
Not Matched
Meaning of the results
Matched: The record passed all admission-number, first-name, username, and account checks.
Review: The record may have a possible match, but it needs a person to check it.
Not Matched: The admission number is missing or was not found in the dump.
Email Mapping Rules
The email-mapping process compares each student's email address and first name with the database records. The following rules are applied in order.
Select the source records:
Use the original school file, or
Use the Not Matched records from admission mapping.
Check that the selected email and first-name columns are available.
Clean the values before comparison:
Remove extra spaces.
Convert email addresses and first names to lowercase.
Capitalization differences are therefore ignored.
Retrieve database records matching the email addresses in the source file.
Check each school record:
If the email address is blank → Not Matched
If the email address is not found in the database → Not Matched
If the same email appears multiple times in the school records → Review
If the email belongs to multiple database records → Review
If the email is found but the school first name is blank → Review
If the email is found but the database first name is blank → Review
If the school and database first names are different → Review
If the first names match but contain only one character → Review
If the email and first name match → Continue to the school check
Confirm that the student belongs to the selected school:
If the selected school index is unavailable → Review
If the student's school is missing in the database → Review
If the student's database school differs from the selected school → Review
If the email, first name, and school all match → Matched
For matched records, copy the username and user ID from the database.
Perform a final duplicate-account check:
If multiple matched students have the same username or user ID, move them to Review.
Separate the final records into three groups:
Matched
Review
Not Matched
Important difference from admission mapping: Email mapping does not first remove completely identical school rows. Repeated nonblank emails are sent to Review.
Meaning of the results
Matched: The email, first name, and selected school match, and the account passes the duplicate check.
Review: A possible record was found, but one or more details require a person to check them.
Not Matched: The email address is missing or was not found in the database.
Full Name + Class Concatenation Rules
The class-concatenation process combines each student's full name and class number and compares the result with the admission dump.
Select the source records:
Original school file
Admission Not Matched records
Email Not Matched records
Check that:
The school records are available.
The admission dump is available.
The selected full-name and class-number columns exist.
The dump contains the required generated comparison column.
Clean the values before comparison:
Remove spaces before and after the full name and class number.
Convert the full name and class number to lowercase.
Remove all spaces inside the full name.
Create the comparison value by joining the cleaned full name and class number.
Example: John Smith + 5 becomes johnsmith5.
Look for the generated value in the admission dump.
Check each student record:
If the full name is blank → Not Matched
If the class number is blank → Not Matched
If no dump record has the same generated value → Not Matched
If multiple dump records have the same generated value → Review
If exactly one dump record has the same generated value → Matched
For matched records, copy the username and user ID from the dump.
Perform a final duplicate-account check:
If multiple matched students have the same username, move them to Review.
If multiple matched students have the same user ID, move them to Review.
Separate the final records into three groups:
Matched
Review
Not Matched
Important: This method only checks the combined full-name and class value. It does not compare the admission number, email address, or individual parts of the name.
Meaning of the results
Matched: Exactly one dump record has the same combined full-name and class value, and the account passes the duplicate check.
Review: Multiple dump records match, or the same username or user ID is assigned to multiple matched students.
Not Matched: The full name or class number is missing, or no dump record has the same combined value.
Sanity Check Rules
Before checking individual columns, extra spaces at the beginning and end of every value are removed. The sanity check reports each row that needs correction.
First Name
First name is required.
It cannot be blank.
Only English letters A–Z are allowed.
Numbers, symbols, punctuation, and spaces are not allowed.
John → Valid
John Paul → Invalid
John2 → Invalid
Last Name
Last name is optional, and a blank value is allowed.
If provided, it can contain only English letters and spaces.
Numbers, punctuation, and other symbols are not allowed.
Smith → Valid
Van Dyke → Valid
Smith2 → Invalid
O'Brien → Invalid
Full Name
The full-name column itself is optional.
If the file contains a full-name column, every row must have a full name.
Only English letters and spaces are allowed.
Numbers, punctuation, and other symbols are not allowed.
John Smith → Valid
John Smith 2 → Invalid
John O'Brien → Invalid
Admission Number
The admission number is displayed in the sanity-check results.
No admission-number format validation is performed at this stage.
Blank or duplicate admission numbers are handled later during admission mapping.
Leading zeros are preserved.
Email
Email is optional during the sanity check, and a blank email is allowed.
If provided, it must follow a normal format such as name@domain.com.
It must contain a value before @, a valid domain after @, and a final extension containing at least two letters.
Duplicate email addresses are not allowed.
Duplicate checking ignores uppercase and lowercase differences.
Every occurrence of a duplicated email is reported.
student@example.com → Valid
student@example → Invalid
student@.com → Invalid
Student@example.com and student@example.com → Duplicate
Gender
If the gender column is present, every row must contain a recognized value.
Accepted values are Male, Female, or Others.
Capitalization does not matter.
Any other value or blank value is reported as invalid.
Class Number
If the class column is present, every row must contain a valid class.
A class can be a recognized class name or a positive whole number greater than zero.
Recognized names are Class I through Class XII, Other, Nursery, LKG, UKG, KG, Pre Nursery, Pre Primary, Pre School, Play Group, and Passed Out.
Capitalization does not matter.
Zero, negative numbers, decimals, and unknown class names are invalid.
Class V → Valid
5 → Valid
0 → Invalid
5.5 → Invalid
Section
The section column is optional.
If the file contains a section column, every row must have a section.
Blank sections are reported.
The sanity check does not validate the section's format or compare it with the database.
House
House is optional, and a blank house is allowed.
If provided, the house must already exist in the database.
Comparison ignores uppercase and lowercase differences.
If the house is not found, the row is reported for correction or house creation.
Username
Username is not validated by this mapping-file sanity check.
Username checks are performed separately during the bulk-registration process.
Other Columns
Columns not listed above are preserved but are not checked.
The sanity check does not remove duplicate rows.
A single row can show more than one problem.
